q: 网络分层（OSI 模型）对应用开发者的根本意义是什么？
q_en: What is the core value of network layering, or the OSI model, for application developers?
options: 规定了所有协议的字节格式
分层是抽象：只需和下一层打交道
让网络传输更快
强制所有系统用 7 层协议
why: 分层就是抽象——像用语言里的 open 而不是手动指挥磁盘读字节。请求网页时你不需要懂物理层，只要会用下一层即可。
why_en: Network layers are abstractions that let developers reason about communication at their own level without knowing how lower layers move the bits.
diagram:
flowchart TB

    B --> C["网络层 L3"]

Layering is an abstraction — you deal only with the layer below you.
It makes network transmission inherently faster.
It forces every system to implement all seven OSI layers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把网络通信拆成 7 层的参考模型，每层只依赖它下面那一层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OSI is the reference model that splits network communication into seven layers, each depending only on the layer below it.

optionExplanations: 分层从没规定过字节格式，那是具体协议自己的事，分层只是把复杂度切开。
分层的价值就是抽象——你只需要弄懂和你相邻的下一层，不用管物理层怎么搬比特。
分层不会让传输本身变快，它换来的是可维护性和职责隔离，不是性能。
没有系统被强制走满 7 层，很多实现会跳过或合并某些层。
optionExplanations_en: layering never dictates byte formats; that's each protocol's own job, layering just splits up complexity.
layering's value is abstraction — you only need the layer right below you, not how bits move on the wire.
layering doesn't speed up transmission itself; it buys maintainability, not performance.
no system is forced to implement all seven layers; real stacks skip or merge layers freely.

q: 网络层（L3）的 IP 协议负责什么？
q_en: What is IP responsible for at the network layer, or L3?
options: 保证数据按序到达
加密通信内容
把数据切成包并尽力而为投递
维护客户端与服务器的会话

why_en: IP handles routing and addressing by breaking data into packets and forwarding them with best-effort delivery to any destination address.
options_en: It guarantees packets arrive in order.
It encrypts the contents of the communication.
It breaks data into packets and delivers them best-effort.
It maintains session state between client and server.

q: 传输层（L4）在网络层之上补充了什么？
q_en: What does the transport layer, or L4, add on top of the network layer?
options: 端到端通信服务：可靠性、有序性等特性
域名解析（DNS 查询）
HTML 页面渲染引擎
物理层的信号调制与编码
why: L3 只把包尽力扔到目的地；TCP/QUIC/UDP 这层决定要不要在其上提供可靠、有序、流控等保证——否则你拿到的就是一堆乱序的包。
why_en: The transport layer adds end-to-end services like reliability, ordering, and flow control on top of the network layer's raw packet delivery.
options_en: End-to-end services like reliability and ordering.
Domain name resolution via DNS queries.
The browser's HTML rendering engine.
Modulating and encoding the physical-layer signal.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Layer 4, the transport layer, provides end-to-end guarantees like reliability, ordering, and flow control, dominated by TCP, UDP, and QUIC.

HTML 渲染发生在浏览器的应用层，传输层根本看不到内容格式。
物理信号调制属于物理层（L1），传输层只处理逻辑上的字节流。

domain resolution is DNS's job at the application layer, unrelated to transport.

signal modulation belongs to the physical layer (L1); transport only handles logical byte streams.

q: 把「浏览器输入 URL 到拿到网页」的步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the browser-to-webpage request flow in the correct order.
steps: TCP 三次握手建立连接
DNS 把域名解析成 IP 地址
服务器处理请求并准备响应
客户端发送 HTTP GET 请求
TCP 四次挥手关闭连接
服务器发回 HTTP 响应
why: DNS 解析 → TCP 握手 → 发请求 → 服务器处理（多数工程师唯一控制的延迟）→ 回响应 → 挥手断开。一次「简单」请求背后是多轮包交换，层层都有延迟。
why_en: A web request resolves DNS, performs the TCP handshake, sends the HTTP request, waits for server processing, receives the response, and tears the connection down.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 客户端
    participant D as DNS
    participant S as 服务器
    C->>D: 域名解析
    D-->>C: IP 地址
    C->>S: SYN / SYN-ACK / ACK（三次握手）
    C->>S: HTTP GET
    S-->>C: HTTP 响应
    C->>S: FIN / ACK / FIN / ACK（四次挥手）

q: 补全 TCP 三次握手：
q_en: Complete the TCP three-way handshake.
text: 客户端发 {{SYN}} 请求连接；服务器回 {{SYN-ACK}} 确认请求；客户端再发 {{ACK}} 完成连接建立。断开则用 FIN/ACK/FIN/ACK 四次挥手。
why: 三次握手建立、四次挥手拆除——每个不复用连接的请求都要重复这套流程，这是后面讨论持久连接和负载均衡的伏笔。
why_en: TCP opens with a SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK three-way handshake and closes with a four-way FIN and ACK exchange.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: SYN
    S-->>C: SYN-ACK
    C->>S: ACK
    Note over C,S: 连接已建立

scenario: 一个 API 网关每秒处理 5 万次短请求，你想把每请求的连接建立开销压下来。
scenario_en: An API gateway handles fifty thousand short requests per second, and you want to cut the per-request connection setup cost.
q: TCP 连接是客户端和服务器都要维护的状态：这一事实带来什么设计影响？
q_en: What design consequence follows from TCP connection state living on both client and server?
options: 连接一旦建立就永远免费
状态只存在服务器端，不在客户端
不用 keep-alive 就要重建连接
TCP 连接不占用任何资源
why: 连接即状态，双方都要维护；不复用就得每请求重建，开销可观。设计实时更新类系统（持久连接）时这一点会反复出现。
why_en: Because a connection is state both sides maintain, every request repeats the costly setup unless you use keep-alive or multiplexing, which matters for realtime systems.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["请求 1"] --> B["建连"]
    B --> C["响应"]
    C --> D["断开"]
    D --> E["请求 2 再建连"]
    C -.keep-alive.-> F["复用连接"]
options_en: Once established, a connection is free forever.
The state only lives on the server, never the client.
Without keep-alive you rebuild the connection every time.
A TCP connection consumes no resources at all.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让一条 TCP 连接被多个 HTTP 请求复用，省去重复握手的开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP keep-alive lets one TCP connection serve multiple HTTP requests, avoiding repeated handshake overhead.

optionExplanations: 维护连接本身要占内存和文件描述符，从来不是免费的，只是分摊到了每次请求。
TCP 是双方对等维护状态，客户端和服务器都要记住序号、窗口，不是只有服务器。
连接状态双方都要维护，不复用连接（没有 keep-alive）就得每次请求重新握手，开销明显。
每条 TCP 连接都占用服务器内存和文件描述符，大量并发连接会实实在在压垮资源。
optionExplanations_en: keeping a connection alive still costs memory and file descriptors — it's amortized, not free.
TCP state is kept by both sides; client and server both track sequence numbers, not just the server.
both sides hold connection state, so without keep-alive you pay a fresh handshake on every request.
every TCP connection consumes real memory and file descriptors; enough of them exhaust resources.

scenario: 你把自建服务部署在公司内网，现在要让互联网上的外部用户直接访问它。
scenario_en: You deployed a self-hosted service inside the corporate network, and now external users on the internet need to reach it directly.
q: 关于公网 IP，正确的说法是？
q_en: Which statement about public IP addresses is correct?
options: 任何人可以随便自封公网 IP 并被全网路由
公网 IP 由 RIR 分配，全网可路由
公网 IP 只在局域网内部有效，出不了本地网络
公网 IP 由 DNS 服务器直接分配给客户端
why: 私有网络里 IP 随便定，但要让互联网流量找到你，必须用 RIR 分配的可路由地址。互联网路由基础设施针对公网 IP 之间的转发做了优化。
why_en: Public IPs are allocated by regional internet registries and are routable, so the internet backbone knows for example that addresses starting with 17 belong to Apple.
options_en: Anyone can self-assign a public IP and have it routed by the whole internet.
Public IPs are allocated by a RIR and are globally routable.
A public IP only works inside a local network and never leaves it.
Public IPs are assigned directly to clients by DNS servers.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP is the network-layer protocol that addresses packets and forwards them across networks on a best-effort basis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责分配可在公网路由的 IP 地址段的区域机构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A RIR is the regional authority that allocates blocks of publicly routable IP addresses.

optionExplanations: 自己乱定的地址不会被互联网骨干路由接受，必须走正规分配才能被全网识别。
公网 IP 由 RIR 统一分配，保证全球唯一、可被互联网路由基础设施转发。
只在局域网内有效的是私有地址段，公网 IP 恰恰是要能被外部路由的地址。
DNS 只负责把域名解析成已有的 IP，它不分配 IP 地址本身。
optionExplanations_en: a self-assigned address won't be accepted by the internet backbone without proper allocation.
public IPs are allocated by RIRs, guaranteeing global uniqueness so routing infrastructure can forward them.
addresses valid only inside a LAN are private ranges — a public IP is exactly one that routes outside.
DNS only resolves a name to an existing IP; it never assigns the IP address itself.

scenario: 为多人对战游戏选传输协议：位置更新每秒 60 次，晚到的包不如直接丢掉。
scenario_en: You're picking a transport for a multiplayer game where position updates fire sixty times a second, and a late packet is worse than a dropped one.
q: UDP 的关键特性有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which properties does UDP have?
options: 无连接：没有握手和连接建立，开销小、延迟低
不保证送达：丢包不会有任何通知
不保证顺序：包可能乱序到达
自动去重，保证恰好一次投递
why: UDP 是「机枪式」spray and pray：在 IP 之上几乎不加功能，换来速度。无连接、可能丢、可能乱序，也没有重复保护——收到的就是一坨二进制加上来源/目的地址端口。
why_en: UDP is connectionless with no handshake, offers no delivery or ordering guarantees, and has lower latency precisely because it adds so little on top of IP.

optionExplanations: 延迟是硬指标时，UDP 省掉握手和重传等待，直接把延迟压到最低。
媒体流丢一帧只是轻微卡顿，能容忍丢失就没必要为完整性支付重传的延迟代价。
遥测/日志量大且偶尔丢几条不影响整体判断时，UDP 的低开销比逐条可靠投递更划算。
浏览器原生不支持裸 UDP，选它前要确认目标端不是普通浏览器，或已准备好替代通道。
optionExplanations_en: when latency is a hard requirement, UDP skips handshake and retransmission waits, keeping it lowest.
losing a media frame is a minor glitch, so tolerable loss removes any reason to pay retransmission latency.
with high-volume telemetry where a few dropped entries don't skew the picture, UDP's low overhead wins.
browsers lack a native raw-UDP API, so confirm the target isn't a plain browser or has a fallback channel.

scenario: 做浏览器视频会议：登录鉴权一次都不能错，音视频帧可以丢但必须低延迟。
scenario_en: You're building a browser video meeting product where login and auth can never fail, but media frames may drop as long as latency stays low.
q: 一个基于 Web 的视频会议应用，典型的协议组合是？
q_en: What protocol mix is typical for a web-based video meeting app?
options: TCP 管信令鉴权，UDP 传音视频
全部走 UDP，包括登录
全部走 TCP，包括视频帧
信令走 UDP，视频走 TCP
why: 现代应用经常混搭：控制面（信令、鉴权）要可靠所以走 TCP/HTTP；媒体面要低延迟、容忍丢帧所以走 UDP/WebRTC。
why_en: A web conferencing app typically uses TCP and HTTP for signaling and authentication but UDP via WebRTC for the audio and video streams.
diagram:
flowchart LR C["客户端"] -->|HTTP/TCP
信令 鉴权| S["服务端"] C <-->|WebRTC/UDP
音视频| P["对端"] P -->|HTTP/TCP
信令| S
optionDiagrams:
flowchart LR
    A["登录/信令"] -->|TCP/HTTP| S["服务端"]
    A <-->|UDP/WebRTC| B["音视频对端"]

flowchart LR
    A["登录"] -->|UDP| S["服务端"]
    A -->|UDP| V["视频"]

flowchart LR
    A["视频帧"] -->|TCP 排队| S["服务端"]

flowchart LR
    A["信令"] -->|UDP| S["服务端"]
    A -->|TCP| V["视频"]
options_en: TCP handles signaling and auth, UDP carries the audio and video.
Everything over UDP, including login.
Everything over TCP, including video frames.
Signaling over UDP, video over TCP.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让浏览器之间直接进行点对点音视频/数据传输的协议族。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebRTC is a protocol suite that lets browsers exchange audio, video, or data directly, peer to peer.

optionExplanations: 登录、鉴权这些控制信息必须完整送达，走可靠的 TCP/HTTP；画面能丢帧换低延迟，走 UDP/WebRTC。
登录鉴权这类必须完整到达的数据不适合 UDP，丢包会直接导致登录失败或状态不一致。
视频帧全走 TCP 会让丢包变成重传排队，卡顿反而更严重，不符合实时媒体的取舍。
这把信令和视频该用的协议完全说反了——信令要可靠该用 TCP，视频要低延迟该用 UDP。
optionExplanations_en: the control plane (login, auth, signaling) needs TCP/HTTP; the media plane needs low-latency UDP/WebRTC.
login and auth data must arrive intact, so UDP isn't suitable — a dropped packet breaks login state.
sending every video frame over TCP turns loss into retransmission queuing, making glitches worse.
this swaps the two — signaling needs TCP's reliability, video needs UDP's low latency.

scenario: 你的 Web 服务要在高峰时从 10 台自动扩到 200 台，实例随时可能被杀掉重建。
scenario_en: Your web service has to autoscale from ten to two hundred instances at peak, with any instance killed and replaced at any moment.
q: 「HTTP 是无状态协议」意味着什么？为什么这是好事？
q_en: What does it mean that HTTP is stateless, and why is that useful?
options: HTTP 不能携带 cookie
每个请求彼此独立，服务器无需记住之前的请求
服务器不能存任何数据
请求之间必须间隔一秒
why: 无状态让服务器可以随意横向扩展、随意替换。系统设计的一般原则：能无状态就无状态，把有状态的表面积压到最小。
why_en: HTTP is stateless because each request is independent, which is good since you want to minimize the stateful surface area of your system.
options_en: HTTP cannot carry cookies.
Each request is independent and the server doesn't need to remember prior requests.
The server cannot store any data.
Requests must be spaced at least a second apart.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

optionExplanations: 无状态跟能不能带 cookie 无关，cookie 只是客户端自己保存、随请求带上的数据。
无状态指每个请求都独立，服务器不用记住上一个请求的上下文，这才让服务器能随意扩展替换。
无状态是「协议不替你记会话」，服务器完全可以存数据，只是不能靠协议本身记住谁是谁。
HTTP 协议本身对请求间隔没有任何强制要求，这条限制根本不存在。
optionExplanations_en: statelessness has nothing to do with cookies — cookies are client-stored data sent with requests.
statelessness means each request stands alone with no remembered context, letting servers scale freely.
statelessness means the protocol itself doesn't track sessions; the server can still store data.
HTTP itself imposes no required gap between requests — that constraint doesn't exist.

scenario: 你在设计公开 API，网关会自动重试「可安全重复」的方法，方法语义必须选对。
scenario_en: You're designing a public API where the gateway auto-retries methods that are safe to repeat, so the method semantics have to be right.
q: 关于 HTTP 请求方法的约定，正确的是？
q_en: Which convention for HTTP methods is correct?
options: POST 按约定应该是幂等的
PUT 是用来删除资源的方法
PATCH 是用来整体替换资源的
GET 幂等无请求体；DELETE 也幂等
why: GET 取数据（幂等、无 body）、POST 提交、PUT 更新、PATCH 部分更新、DELETE 删除（幂等）。方法和状态码像枚举一样标准化。
why_en: GET requests should be idempotent and carry no body, and DELETE requests should be idempotent as well.
options_en: POST should conventionally be idempotent.
PUT is the method used to delete a resource.
PATCH is the method used to fully replace a resource.
GET is idempotent with no body; DELETE is idempotent too.
codeSample:
GET    /orders/42        HTTP/1.1   # 幂等，无 body，重复调用结果一致
POST   /orders           HTTP/1.1   # 创建新资源，不是幂等的
DELETE /orders/42        HTTP/1.1   # 幂等：删一次和删十次效果相同

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

optionExplanations: POST 按约定是非幂等的，重复提交会创建多个资源，这正是它和 PUT 的关键区别。
PUT 是整体更新（或创建）资源，删除资源对应的是 DELETE。
整体替换资源是 PUT 的职责，PATCH 按约定是部分更新。
GET 只读无请求体、重复调用不产生副作用；DELETE 重复调用效果一样，两者都是幂等操作。
optionExplanations_en: POST is conventionally non-idempotent — repeating it creates duplicates, unlike PUT.
PUT replaces (or creates) a resource wholesale; deleting one is DELETE's job.
replacing a resource wholesale is PUT's job; PATCH is conventionally a partial update.
GET is read-only with no side effect on repeat, and DELETE has the same end state on repeat — both idempotent.

q: 补全常见 HTTP 状态码：
q_en: Fill in the common HTTP status-code families.
text: {{200}} OK 成功；{{201}} Created 创建成功；301 永久移动；{{404}} Not Found 未找到；401 未认证；{{429}} Too Many Requests 触发限流；502 Bad Gateway 上游返回无效响应。
why: 2xx 成功、3xx 移动、4xx 客户端错、5xx 服务端错。429（限流）和 502（上游坏响应）在系统设计讨论里出镜率最高。
why_en: Two hundred means success, two-oh-one created, four-oh-four not found, four-twenty-nine rate limited, and five-oh-two a bad response from the upstream server.

scenario: 你要设计一个多年不破坏兼容的 API 头部，老客户端不认新压缩算法也不能挂。
scenario_en: You need an API header design that stays compatible for years, so old clients that don't know a new compression algorithm still keep working.
q: HTTP 的内容协商（如 Accept-Encoding）为什么被拿来当 API 设计的范例？
q_en: Why is HTTP content negotiation, such as Accept-Encoding, a useful API design example?
options: 因为它强制所有客户端用 gzip
客户端声明能处理的编码，服务器选优编码返回
因为它是唯一的 HTTP 头
因为它能加密数据
why: 头部是灵活的键值对，Accept-Encoding 展示了如何设计对未知未来用例友好的接口：能力协商、向后兼容、优雅降级——HTTP 规范务实哲学的缩影。
why_en: Content negotiation lets clients advertise supported encodings so servers respond with the most efficient one, giving both backward compatibility and graceful degradation.
options_en: Because it forces every client to use gzip.
The client declares which encodings it supports, and the server returns its best pick.
Because it's the only HTTP header that exists.
Because it encrypts the data.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 响应头，标明服务器实际用了哪种压缩编码（如 gzip）返回内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Content-Encoding is the HTTP response header stating which compression, like gzip, the server actually used for the body.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

optionExplanations: 它不强制任何编码——只是客户端表达自己支持哪些，服务器完全可以选择不压缩。
客户端在头里声明自己能处理哪些编码，服务器从中选一个最优返回——这是能力协商、向后兼容的范例。
HTTP 头有几十个（Content-Type、Authorization 等）；这只是其中一个，不是唯一存在的头。
编码协商跟加密无关：加密是 TLS/HTTPS 的职责，这个头只管压缩格式的协商。
optionExplanations_en: Accept-Encoding doesn't force any encoding — the client just states support, server can pick none.
the client declares supported encodings and the server picks the best match — capability negotiation.
HTTP has dozens of headers (Content-Type, Authorization); Accept-Encoding is just one of them.
encoding negotiation is unrelated to encryption; that's TLS/HTTPS's job, not Accept-Encoding's.

scenario: 你的登录接口在公共 WiFi 上被抓包，密码明文可见，要在协议层把这个洞堵上。
scenario_en: Your login endpoint got sniffed on public WiFi with the password visible in plaintext, and you need a protocol-level fix.
q: HTTPS 在 HTTP 之上加了什么？
q_en: What does HTTPS add on top of HTTP?
options: TLS/SSL 安全层：加密防窃听
一层负责压缩响应体积的压缩层
一层缓存热点数据的缓存层
一层做请求分发的负载均衡层
why: HTTPS = HTTP + TLS/SSL，请求响应内容在传输中被加密。做公开网站，用 HTTPS 没有商量余地。
why_en: HTTPS adds a TLS security layer that encrypts communications against eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks, and public websites use it without exception.
options_en: A TLS/SSL security layer that encrypts against eavesdropping.
A compression layer that shrinks the response body.
A caching layer that stores hot data.
A load-balancing layer that spreads requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 HTTP 之上加一层 TLS/SSL 加密，防窃听和中间人攻击。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTPS layers TLS/SSL encryption on top of HTTP to prevent eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks.

termDefinitions.fullName: Transport Layer Security / Secure Sockets Layer
termDefinitions.meaning: 给网络连接加密和身份验证的协议，SSL 是 TLS 的前身。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TLS, the successor to SSL, encrypts and authenticates a network connection.

optionExplanations: HTTPS 就是在 HTTP 基础上加一层 TLS/SSL，把传输内容加密，防止被中间人窃听或篡改。
压缩由 Accept-Encoding 之类机制处理，跟 HTTPS 加的这层安全能力是两回事。
缓存靠 Cache-Control、CDN 等机制实现，HTTPS 本身不提供缓存能力。
负载均衡是独立的架构组件，跟 HTTP 加密与否没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: HTTPS adds a TLS/SSL layer over HTTP that encrypts content, preventing eavesdropping or tampering.
compression is handled by mechanisms like Accept-Encoding, unrelated to HTTPS's security layer.
caching comes from Cache-Control or a CDN — HTTPS itself provides no caching capability.
load balancing is a separate architectural component, unrelated to HTTP encryption.

scenario: 转账 API 全站已上 HTTPS，但请求体里带的 userId 依然能被客户端随意改。
scenario_en: Your transfer API is fully on HTTPS, yet the userId carried in the request body can still be freely tampered with by the client.
q: HTTPS 加密了传输内容，但一个常见的安全错误依然存在——是什么？
q_en: What common security mistake still exists even when HTTPS encrypts traffic in transit?
options: 忘记按时续期证书，导致证书过期失效
用了太旧、早已被淘汰的 TLS 协议版本
把用户密码明文直接写进了请求 URL 参数里
信任请求体内容，如直接用 user ID 查库
why: 加密保护「传输中」不被偷看，但不保证内容是你的客户端生成的。API 永远不要信任未经校验的请求体，也别索要你无法验证的东西。
why_en: Encryption does not make request contents trustworthy, so never use an unvalidated user id from the request body or an attacker can read arbitrary data.
options_en: Forgetting to renew the certificate on time, so it lapses.
Using an outdated TLS version that was deprecated long ago.
Putting a user's password in plaintext right inside the request URL.
Trusting the request body's contents, like using a raw user id to query the database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 HTTP 之上加一层 TLS/SSL 加密，防窃听和中间人攻击。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTPS layers TLS/SSL encryption on top of HTTP to prevent eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks.

optionExplanations: 证书过期确实是常见运维事故，但它不是「加密了传输却仍不安全」这条思路要指的错误。
旧版 TLS 是配置层面的疏漏，跟这里说的「加密内容却还有安全漏洞」不是同一类问题。
把密码写进 URL 确实是坏习惯，但 HTTPS 下它同样被加密，风险在于 URL 会被日志、浏览器历史留存，属于另一类问题。
HTTPS 只保证传输不被偷看，不保证请求体真的来自可信客户端；直接信任 user ID 查库，攻击者照样能伪造。
optionExplanations_en: Certificate expiry is a real ops failure, but not the mistake that survives even with encryption turned on.
An outdated TLS version is a config gap, a different category from the mistake described here.
Putting a password in the URL is a bad habit, but HTTPS still encrypts it — the risk is URLs landing in logs and history, a different category.
HTTPS only protects transit, not whether the body is genuinely trusted — trusting a user ID lets it be forged.

scenario: 面试里要为服务间/对外通信定 API 范式，没有特别的灵活性或极端性能诉求。
scenario_en: In an interview, you need an API style for service-to-service or public communication, without unusual flexibility or extreme performance needs.
q: 该默认选哪个？
q_en: Which API style should you use by default in this interview setting?
options: GraphQL
REST：简单灵活，通用基线
gRPC
自定义二进制协议
why: 像 TCP 一样，REST 是面试的推荐默认值。核心思想：客户端对「资源」做简单操作。你的 Core Entities 往往直接映射成 API 资源。
why_en: REST is the recommended default API paradigm for interviews, and you reach for GraphQL, gRPC, SSE, or WebSockets only when REST cannot meet a specific need.
whenOtherWins: 前端需求快速变化/刻意不定 → GraphQL；内部高性能服务间通信 → gRPC；服务器推送 → SSE/WebSocket。
options_en: GraphQL.
REST: simple, flexible, a universal baseline.
gRPC.
A custom binary protocol.
tradeoff: REST 简单通用默认 vs GraphQL/gRPC 满足特定诉求

rows: 默认，通用 Web/服务 API
内部高性能服务间通信

termDefinitions.meaning: 把系统建模成「资源」、用标准 HTTP 方法操作它们的 API 风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that models a system as resources manipulated with standard HTTP verbs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种查询语言和 API 范式，客户端在一次请求里精确声明需要哪些字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a query language and API paradigm that lets clients specify exactly which fields they need in a single request.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 发起的高性能 RPC 框架，基于 HTTP/2 和 Protocol Buffers 二进制序列化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is Google's high-performance RPC framework built on HTTP/2 and Protocol Buffers binary serialization.

optionExplanations: GraphQL 适合前端需求高度多变、想灵活查询任意字段组合的场景，没这个诉求时它只会多一层复杂度。
没有特殊诉求时 REST 是面试的推荐默认——把 Core Entities 直接映射成资源，用 HTTP 动词表达操作。
gRPC 在内部高性能服务间通信上更强，但二进制协议和工具链对外部场景不友好，不该是默认起点。
自定义二进制协议能榨干性能，但开发维护成本远超收益，除非有极端性能诉求，否则是过度设计。
optionExplanations_en: GraphQL fits frontends wanting flexible field queries; without that need it's just extra complexity.
with no special requirement, REST is the default — map core entities to resources, verbs to actions.
gRPC is stronger for internal high-performance calls, but its binary protocol is unfriendly to external use.
A custom binary protocol squeezes out speed, but its build cost dwarfs the benefit absent an extreme need.

scenario: 你要为 Web/iOS/Android 共用的同一个后端定接口规范，希望语义可预测、好缓存。
scenario_en: You're defining one API convention for a single backend shared by web, iOS, and Android, and you want semantics that are predictable and cacheable.
q: REST 的核心建模原则是什么？
q_en: What is the core modeling principle behind REST?
options: 把所有操作做成 POST /doAction
每个页面一个专属 API
围绕「资源」建模，用 HTTP 动词+路径表达操作
把数据库 schema 直接暴露给客户端
why: REST 的世界观：客户端对资源做操作。HTTP 方法当动词、路径定位资源、JSON 作载体（非强制）；嵌套路径如 GET /users/{id}/posts 表达资源关系。
why_en: REST models everything as resources acted on by HTTP verbs with path conventions, typically exchanging JSON representations.
options_en: Make every operation a POST /doAction.
Give every page its own dedicated API.
Model everything around resources, expressed with HTTP verbs plus path conventions.
Expose the database schema directly to clients.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把系统建模成「资源」、用标准 HTTP 方法操作它们的 API 风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that models a system as resources manipulated with standard HTTP verbs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的文本序列化格式，键值对结构、人类可读但比二进制格式占空间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JSON is a common text-based serialization format that is human-readable but bulkier than binary formats.

optionExplanations: 把所有操作塞进 POST /doAction 是典型的 RPC 化写法，恰恰违背了 REST 围绕资源建模的原则。
为每个页面单独写 API 会让接口和前端强耦合，REST 提倡围绕资源而不是页面设计接口。
REST 把系统看成一堆资源，用动词化的方法操作它、用路径当定位符，嵌套路径还能表达资源间的从属关系。
直接暴露数据库 schema 会让客户端和内部实现强耦合，资源模型应该是对外的抽象。
optionExplanations_en: cramming actions into POST /doAction is classic RPC-style, exactly what resource modeling avoids.
a bespoke API per page tightly couples interface to frontend — REST models around resources, not pages.
REST treats the system as 'resources' — HTTP verbs act as verbs, paths locate resources and relationships.
exposing the database schema couples clients to internals — the resource model should be an abstraction.

scenario: 代码评审里出现 POST /updateUser、POST /startGame，你要按 REST 规范给出改法。
scenario_en: Code review turns up POST /updateUser and POST /startGame, and you need to remodel them the RESTful way.
q: 工程师常想出 updateUser、startGame 这样的接口名，RESTful 的改法是？
q_en: How would REST remodel operation-style endpoints like updateUser or startGame?
options: 变成 PUT /users/{id} 和 PATCH /games
POST /updateUser 和 POST /startGame
GET /users/update
保持原名，REST 不管命名
why: updateUser、startGame 是「操作」不是「资源」，不 RESTful。REST 思维是找到背后的资源（user、game）再用标准 HTTP 动词表达变更。
why_en: Operations like updateUser become PUT on the user resource, and startGame becomes a PATCH setting the game's status, because REST thinks in resources not operations.
codeSample:

scenario: 面试中考虑是否用 WebRTC。它出了名地难做对，连最好的实现也会掉线。
scenario_en: You are considering WebRTC in an interview. It is famously hard to get right, and even strong implementations can disconnect.
q: 对候选人最稳妥的使用边界是？
q_en: What is the safest interview boundary for using WebRTC?
options: 任何实时应用都用 WebRTC
所有协作编辑器都用 WebRTC
只把 WebRTC 用于音视频通话/会议
彻底不学 WebRTC

why_en: Stick to WebRTC for audio and video calling and conferencing, because most problems do not need peer-to-peer and candidates go wildly off trail trying.

options_en: Use WebRTC for any real-time application.
Use WebRTC for every collaborative editor.
Reserve WebRTC for audio/video calling and conferencing.
Never learn WebRTC at all.
tradeoff: WebRTC 真 P2P 但难做对 vs WebSocket+中心服务器更稳妥

optionExplanations: 多数「实时」需求根本不需要真 P2P，硬上 WebRTC 只会引入它出了名难搞的连接和 NAT 穿透问题。

低延迟直连的收益在通话/会议场景里明显超过连接难做对的代价，这才是它的合理边界。
完全不学不可取——面试如果聊到实时音视频，WebRTC 仍然是候选人该知道的标准答案。
optionExplanations_en: Most 'real-time' needs don't need true P2P — WebRTC just imports its notorious connection headaches.
Collaborative editors need stored state and multi-party sync, better suited to WebSocket plus a server.
audio/video calls are WebRTC's legitimate home — the low-latency payoff outweighs the connection difficulty.
Skipping it entirely isn't wise — real-time audio/video interviews still expect candidates to know WebRTC.

scenario: 你的单机服务已经吃满 CPU，面试官问下一步怎么扩，只剩 20 分钟画架构。
scenario_en: Your single-machine service is CPU-saturated, the interviewer asks how you'd scale next, and only twenty minutes are left to draw the architecture.
q: 垂直扩展 vs 水平扩展，以及面试中的现实是？
q_en: How should you compare vertical and horizontal scaling in interviews?
options: 垂直=加更多机器，水平=换更大的机器
垂直换大机器，水平加机器；面试常见水平扩展
两者的具体做法完全一模一样
水平扩展从来都不需要负载均衡
why: 现代硬件强到「几台大机器顶过去几千台小机器」，但面试的常规剧本还是水平扩展。往白板上加机器前，得先回答「客户端跟谁说话」——即负载均衡。
why_en: Vertical scaling means bigger servers and horizontal means more servers, and while modern hardware favors vertical, interviews almost always end up horizontal with load balancing.
options_en: Vertical means adding more machines, horizontal means switching to a bigger machine.
Vertical means a bigger machine, horizontal means more machines; interviews mostly land on horizontal.
The two approaches are entirely identical in every way.
Horizontal scaling never, ever needs a load balancer.
tradeoff: 垂直扩展简单但有上限 vs 水平扩展无上限但要做负载均衡

termDefinitions.meaning: 把请求分发到多台后端服务器、并监控它们健康状态的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer is the component that distributes requests across multiple backend servers and monitors their health.

optionExplanations: 这把垂直和水平扩展的定义完全说反了——垂直是换更大的机器，水平才是加更多机器。
垂直扩展是换更大的机器，水平扩展是加更多机器；面试常规剧本仍是水平扩展，因为它没有单机硬件上限。
两种扩展方式的做法、上限和额外基建需求完全不同，不能混为一谈。
一旦有多台机器分担流量，就得先回答「客户端跟谁说话」，这正是负载均衡要解决的问题。
optionExplanations_en: this flips the two definitions — vertical means a bigger machine, horizontal means more machines.
vertical means a bigger machine, horizontal means more machines; interviews default to horizontal.
the two approaches differ completely in method, ceiling, and infrastructure needed.
multiple machines sharing traffic immediately raises 'who does the client talk to' — load balancing.

scenario: 内部服务间调用每秒百万次，多一跳集中式 LB 就多一份延迟和单点风险。
scenario_en: Internal service-to-service calls run at a million per second, and every extra hop through a central load balancer adds latency and a single point of failure.
q: 客户端负载均衡是怎么工作的？优势是什么？
q_en: How does client-side load balancing work, and what is its advantage?
options: 客户端把每个请求都发给中心代理，由它转发
服务器靠随机拒绝请求来实现负载均衡
全部由 DNS 服务器负责处理所有路由决策
客户端从服务注册中心拿服务器列表、自己决定连谁
why: 客户端自己做决策：先向注册中心/目录要可用服务器列表，然后直连目标。快且高效——不用每个请求都过一遍负载均衡器，只要定期（或被推送）更新列表。
why_en: In client-side load balancing the client fetches the server list from a registry and picks a server itself, avoiding an extra network hop on every request.
options_en: The client sends every request to a central proxy that forwards them.
The server balances load by randomly rejecting some requests.
The DNS server alone handles every single routing decision.
The client fetches the server list from a service registry and decides itself which one to call.
tradeoff: 客户端自决省一跳 vs 依赖注册中心同步及时性

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录当前有哪些可用服务器实例及其地址的目录服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A service registry is the directory service that tracks which server instances are currently available and where they are.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把请求分发到多台后端服务器、并监控它们健康状态的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer is the component that distributes requests across multiple backend servers and monitors their health.

optionExplanations: 把请求发给中心代理转发正是「服务端负载均衡」的做法，跟客户端负载均衡的定义相反。
随机拒绝请求不是负载均衡的实现方式，那只会制造无谓的失败。
DNS 只是客户端负载均衡里的一种实现手段（轮转 IP），不是「处理所有路由」的中心角色。
客户端先向注册中心要一份可用服务器列表，再自己挑一台直连，省掉了过一遍中心 LB 的那一跳。
optionExplanations_en: sending requests to a central proxy is server-side load balancing, the opposite of client-side.
randomly rejecting requests isn't a load-balancing technique — it just creates needless failures.
DNS is one implementation of client-side balancing (rotating IPs), not a central routing role.
the client asks a registry for a server list, then connects directly, skipping the hop through a central LB.

rows: 靠列表刷新周期，有延迟
LB 主动健康检查，更快

scenario: Redis 集群把数据分到 16384 个槽，客户端要在一次网络往返内命中正确的分片节点。
scenario_en: A Redis cluster spreads data across 16384 slots, and the client has to hit the right shard node within a single round trip.
q: Redis Cluster 是客户端负载均衡的好例子，它如何运作？
q_en: How does Redis Cluster demonstrate client-side load balancing?
options: 哈希 key 直连，错了收到 MOVED
有一个中央路由服务器分发所有请求
客户端每次随机连一个节点碰运气
用 DNS 轮转决定分片
why: Redis Cluster：gossip 让每个节点掌握全集群拓扑；客户端先问任一节点拿到节点+分片信息，之后 hash key → 定分片 → 直连；发错了节点会回 MOVED 告诉你去哪。
why_en: Redis Cluster nodes gossip cluster state, clients hash the key to pick the shard and connect directly, and a wrong node helpfully replies with MOVED.
options_en: It hashes the key to connect directly, getting MOVED if wrong.
A central router server dispatches every request.
The client connects to a random node and hopes for the best.
DNS round robin decides the shard.
codeSample:
> GET user:1000:profile
(error) MOVED 3999 127.0.0.1:6381
# 客户端按提示重连 6381 端口，并把这个 slot 的归属缓存在本地

termDefinitions.meaning: 节点间两两随机交换状态信息、让全网逐渐收敛到一致视图的通信方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A gossip protocol lets nodes randomly exchange state with each other until the whole cluster converges on a consistent view.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Cluster 返回的重定向响应，告诉客户端目标 key 实际在哪个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MOVED is the redirect response Redis Cluster returns to tell the client which node actually owns a key.

optionExplanations: 客户端对 key 做哈希算出该去哪个分片，直接连对应节点；连错了会收到 MOVED，告诉它去哪重试。
Redis Cluster 没有中央路由服务器，节点靠 gossip 协议互相同步拓扑，客户端直连节点。
随机连节点大概率连错分片，Redis Cluster 靠哈希槽而不是运气来定位数据。
分片是靠哈希槽（hash slot）分配决定的，跟 DNS 轮转毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: the client hashes the key to find its shard and connects directly; a wrong guess gets a MOVED redirect.
Redis Cluster has no central router — nodes sync topology via gossip, clients connect directly.
randomly picking a node likely hits the wrong shard; Cluster locates data via hash slots, not luck.
shard assignment comes from hash slots, unrelated to DNS round-robin.

scenario: 你的两台负载均衡器本身成了单点，而你不想再加一层设备来给它们分流。
scenario_en: Your two load balancers have themselves become a single point of failure, and you don't want yet another device sitting in front of them.
q: DNS 如何充当「客户端负载均衡器」？这还顺带解决了什么经典问题？
q_en: How can DNS act as a client-side load balancer, and what classic problem does that help solve?
options: DNS 会实时检测每台服务器的负载并智能路由
DNS 会主动把请求转发给当前最空闲的那台服务器
DNS 轮转 IP 列表分散流量，也消除 LB 单点
DNS 会把所有的响应内容都缓存下来
why: 每次解析返回不同排序（甚至不同集合）的 IP，客户端自然分散。这也是 LB 单点问题的标准答案：两台 LB 异地部署 + DNS 轮转，一台挂了客户端自动试另一台。
why_en: DNS rotates the list of IPs it returns so clients hit different servers, which is also how you avoid a single point of failure by rotating between two load balancers.
options_en: DNS detects each server's real-time load and intelligently routes to it.
DNS actively forwards the request to whichever server is currently least busy.
DNS rotates the IP list to spread traffic, which also removes the LB single point of failure.
DNS caches every single response it ever returns.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析成 IP 地址的分布式查找系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS is the distributed lookup system that resolves domain names into IP addresses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目或 DNS 记录被视为有效的最长时间，过期后必须刷新。

optionExplanations: 普通 DNS 不检测服务器实时负载，它只是按配置轮转返回的 IP 顺序或集合。
DNS 不转发请求，它只做名字到 IP 的解析，请求本身是客户端自己发出去的。
DNS 每次解析返回不同顺序的 IP，客户端自然分散连接；两台 LB 异地部署配合 DNS 轮转还能消除单点。
DNS 缓存跟这里说的「轮转分散流量」是两码事，缓存行为由 TTL 控制，不是「缓存所有响应」。
optionExplanations_en: plain DNS doesn't monitor real-time load — it rotates the order or set of IPs per configuration.
DNS doesn't forward requests — it only resolves names to IPs; the client sends the actual request.
each lookup returns IPs in a different order, spreading connections; pairing two LBs with DNS also kills SPOF.
DNS caching is separate from 'rotate to spread traffic' — caching is governed by TTL, not this.

scenario: 判断客户端负载均衡适不适合你的系统。
scenario_en: You need to decide whether client-side load balancing fits your system.
q: 它在哪两类场景下工作得好？
q_en: In what two situations does client-side load balancing work well?
options: 任何存在负载均衡需求的场景都适用
少量受控客户端，或能容忍慢更新的大量客户端
只适合纯粹的单体应用架构
只适合纯移动端的应用场景
why: 受控的少量客户端推送更新很容易；海量客户端时更新耗时随客户端数增长，只能靠 TTL 类机制容忍慢更新。面试里内部微服务间用客户端 LB 表现非常好（gRPC 内置）。
why_en: Client-side load balancing works with a small number of controlled clients like internal gRPC services, or many clients that tolerate slow updates like DNS.
whenOtherWins: 大量不受控客户端 + 需要快速感知服务器变化 → 用专用（服务端）负载均衡器。
options_en: Any scenario that has a load-balancing need whatsoever.
A small controlled set of clients, or many clients that can tolerate slow updates.
Only purely monolithic application architectures.
Only purely mobile-only application scenarios.
tradeoff: 少量受控客户端自决 vs 大量客户端靠 TTL 容忍慢更新

rows: 少量受控 或 海量能忍慢

termDefinitions.meaning: 把请求分发到多台后端服务器、并监控它们健康状态的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer is the component that distributes requests across multiple backend servers and monitors their health.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析成 IP 地址的分布式查找系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS is the distributed lookup system that resolves domain names into IP addresses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目或 DNS 记录被视为有效的最长时间，过期后必须刷新。

optionExplanations: 客户端负载均衡不是万能默认——客户端数量大且需要快速感知变化时，靠客户端自己维护列表反而不可靠。
客户端数量少而受控时推送更新很容易；数量大但能接受慢更新（靠 TTL 容忍）时也行得通——这是它的适用场景。
客户端负载均衡跟应用是不是单体没有关系，它描述的是「谁来决定连哪台服务器」，微服务里同样常见。
客户端负载均衡不限于移动端，内部微服务间调用（如 gRPC 内置）是它更典型的场景。
optionExplanations_en: Client-side balancing isn't universal — many clients needing fast updates makes self-kept lists unreliable.
few controlled clients make pushing updates easy; many clients tolerating slow (TTL-based) updates also work.
Client-side balancing has nothing to do with monolith versus microservice — it's about who picks the server.
Client-side balancing isn't mobile-only — internal service calls, built into gRPC, are the typical case.

scenario: 一台后端宕机要立刻摘掉，但它的 IP 早已通过 DNS 分发给了全球客户端。
scenario_en: A backend dies and has to be pulled right away, but its IP was already handed out to clients worldwide through DNS.
q: DNS 的 TTL 机制给「更新服务器列表」带来什么硬约束？
q_en: What hard constraint does DNS TTL create when updating server lists?
options: 远端 DNS 服务器会按 TTL 缓存解析记录
TTL 越长，更新反而传播得越快
TTL 完全不影响更新速度
TTL 只对 HTTPS 流量有影响
why: TTL 是把双刃剑：允许各地 DNS 缓存（扩展性好），但也决定了摘掉一台坏服务器最长要等一个 TTL 才对所有客户端生效。
why_en: DNS entries are cached for their TTL by resolvers everywhere, so your updates cannot propagate to clients faster than that TTL.
options_en: DNS resolvers everywhere cache a record for its TTL.
A longer TTL makes updates propagate even faster.
TTL has no effect on update speed at all.
TTL only affects HTTPS traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析成 IP 地址的分布式查找系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS is the distributed lookup system that resolves domain names into IP addresses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目或 DNS 记录被视为有效的最长时间，过期后必须刷新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the maximum time a cached value or DNS record is considered valid before it must be refreshed.

optionExplanations: TTL 决定了各地 DNS 缓存解析结果的时长，也意味着摘除一台坏节点最多要等满一个周期才对全体客户端生效。
TTL 越长意味着缓存越久不刷新，更新反而传播得更慢，不是更快。
TTL 直接决定了缓存过期前客户端看到的还是旧记录，对更新速度影响很大。
TTL 是 DNS 解析记录的缓存时间，跟走不走 HTTPS 完全无关，任何基于该记录的流量都受它影响。
optionExplanations_en: TTL determines how long resolvers cache a result, so removing a bad server can take up to one full TTL.
a longer TTL means the cache stays stale longer, so updates propagate more slowly, not faster.
TTL directly governs how long clients keep seeing the old record — it strongly affects update speed.
TTL is a DNS record's cache lifetime, unrelated to HTTPS — it affects any traffic relying on it.

scenario: 为 WebSocket 长连接选负载均衡器：同一条连接必须始终落在同一台后端上。
scenario_en: You're picking a load balancer for long-lived WebSocket connections, where a single connection must always land on the same backend.
q: Layer 4 负载均衡器的工作方式是？
q_en: How does a Layer 4 load balancer work?
options: 解析 HTTP 请求内容再路由
只做 DNS 解析
工作在传输层：只看 IP/端口做路由
在应用层重写每个请求
why: L4 LB 几乎不拆包，快而高效；建立的 TCP 连接具有粘性（同连接同后端），概念上就像客户端和那台服务器直连——这正是持久连接协议需要的。
why_en: A layer four load balancer routes on IP and port without inspecting content, acting as if the client had a direct persistent TCP connection to one backend.
options_en: It parses HTTP request content to route.
It only does DNS resolution.
It operates at the transport layer, routing only on IP and port.
It rewrites every request at the application layer.

termDefinitions.meaning: OSI 模型里提供端到端保证（可靠性、顺序、流控）的传输层，主角是 TCP/UDP/QUIC。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Layer 4, the transport layer, provides end-to-end guarantees like reliability, ordering, and flow control, dominated by TCP, UDP, and QUIC.

终止连接，按 HTTP 内容路由
只按源 IP 路由
只能用于 UDP

It terminates the connection and routes on HTTP content.
It only routes by source IP.
It only works with UDP.

an L7 load balancer receives the HTTP request and forwards it based on content like path or cookie.

q_en: Which load balancer type should you choose for WebSocket traffic?
options: 无所谓，选哪一种其实都一样
只能用 DNS 轮转这一种办法来做
选 L7，因为它的功能明显更多
L4 负载均衡器：维持持久 TCP 连接
why: 经验法则：WebSocket → L4（持久连接粘住同一后端）；其余 HTTP 流量（包括长轮询）→ L7 更灵活。个别 L7 LB 也显式支持连接型协议，但一般 L4 是稳妥答案。
why_en: Use a layer four load balancer for WebSockets because it maintains persistent TCP connections to a consistent server, while layer seven suits HTTP-based traffic.
whenOtherWins: 普通 HTTP/REST/SSE 长轮询等流量选 L7：能按内容路由、做 API 网关式的分流。
options_en: It doesn't matter at all, they're fully interchangeable.
You can only use DNS rotation for this, nothing else.
Pick L7, since it clearly has more features.
A layer 4 load balancer, which keeps a persistent TCP connection.
tradeoff: L4 持久连接粘性 vs L7 按内容灵活路由

DNS 轮转能分散初始连接目标，但没法在连接建立后感知服务器健康状况，不能替代专门的负载均衡器。
L7 功能更丰富，但代价是要拆包终止连接，对本该保持粘性的持久 TCP 连接反而不是最优选择。
WebSocket 需要一条连接稳定粘在同一后端，L4 几乎不拆包、只按 IP/端口转发，天然适合维持这种持久连接。
optionExplanations_en: The two LB types behave differently with persistent connections — picking wrong hurts connection stability.
DNS round-robin spreads initial targets but can't sense health after connecting, no substitute for a real LB.
L7 offers richer features, but terminating the link is wrong for a TCP connection that should stay pinned.
WebSocket needs a connection pinned to one backend, and L4 barely inspects packets — a natural fit.

q: L4 与 L7 负载均衡器的一句话对比是？
q_en: What is the one-line comparison between L4 and L7 load balancers?
options: L4 不看内容快转发；L7 按内容智能路由
L4 更智能，反而 L7 更快
两者都会终止 TCP 连接
L7 完全不支持 HTTP
why: 一条性能与智能的取舍线：L4 = 快、透传、连接粘性；L7 = 灵活、内容路由、代价是包检查的 CPU。按「要不要持久连接、要不要按内容分流」来选。
why_en: Layer four is fast and content-blind with persistent connections, while layer seven terminates connections and routes intelligently on request content at higher CPU cost.
options_en: L4 forwards fast without looking at content; L7 routes intelligently on content.
L4 is the smarter one, and L7 is the faster one.
Both of them terminate the TCP connection.
L7 doesn't support HTTP at all.
tradeoff: L4 快但看不到内容 vs L7 智能但更耗 CPU

这把两者的能力描述对调了——更智能、能看内容的是 L7，转发更快的是 L4。
L4 通常不终止连接，效果更像透传，只有 L7 才会终止连接再重新发起。

this swaps the two — L7 is the smarter one that sees content, L4 is the faster one.
L4 typically doesn't terminate the connection, behaving like a pass-through; only L7 terminates it.
L7 is built specifically around protocols like HTTP — supporting HTTP is exactly its home turf.

scenario: 凌晨三点一台后端进程假死但端口还在监听，你不想让值班同学被叫醒手动摘流。
scenario_en: At three in the morning a backend process hangs while still holding its port open, and you don't want on-call paged to drain it by hand.
q: 负载均衡器靠什么实现自动故障转移（高可用的关键）？
q_en: How do load balancers implement automatic failover for high availability?
options: 靠人工值守切换
健康检查：TCP/L7 探测存活
把所有服务器都重启一遍
把流量全部缓存起来
why: LB 不只分流量，还持续监控后端健康：服务器崩溃或断电就停止向它路由，恢复了再加回来。检测并绕开故障、无需人工干预——这是 LB 之于高可用的价值。
why_en: Load balancers run health checks, like TCP connection tests or HTTP checks expecting a 200, and automatically route around servers that fail until they recover.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    LB["LB"] -->|健康检查| A["Server A OK"]
    LB -->|健康检查失败| B["Server B"]
    B -.摘除.-> X["不接流量"]
    A --> U["用户请求"]
options_en: A human manually flips traffic over.
Health checks: a TCP or L7 probe for liveness.
Restart every single server.
Cache all of the traffic.
codeSample:
GET /health HTTP/1.1
Host: backend-3

HTTP/1.1 200 OK   # 健康，继续接流量

termDefinitions.meaning: 负载均衡器定期探测后端是否存活/正常响应，失败就摘掉流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A health check is the load balancer periodically probing whether a backend is alive and responding correctly, pulling traffic if it fails.

optionExplanations: 人工值守切换太慢，达不到自动故障转移的要求，这不是负载均衡器实现高可用的方式。
负载均衡器持续探测后端是否存活，一旦发现故障就停止路由、恢复后再加回来，全程无需人工干预。
重启所有服务器代价太大也没必要，健康检查只需摘掉出问题的那台，其余不受影响。
缓存流量解决的是重复读请求的问题，跟检测和绕开故障服务器完全是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: manual on-call switching is too slow to count as automatic failover.
the LB keeps probing backends; the moment one fails it stops routing to it and re-adds it once recovered.
restarting every server is costly and unnecessary — health checks only need to pull the failing one.
caching traffic solves a repeated-read problem, unrelated to detecting a failed server.

q: 补全常见负载均衡算法：
q_en: Fill in the common load-balancing algorithms.
text: {{Round Robin}}：按顺序轮流分发；Random：随机分发；{{Least Connections}}：发给活跃连接最少的服务器；Least Response Time：发给响应最快的；{{IP Hash}}：按客户端 IP 决定服务器，可用于会话保持。
why: 无状态应用用轮询/随机就好——新服务器加入后自然开始分到流量；持久连接服务用最少连接；要会话粘性用 IP Hash。
why_en: Round robin cycles through servers, least connections picks the server with the fewest active connections, and IP hash maps a client to a consistent server for session persistence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定顺序轮流把请求分给每台服务器的负载均衡算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Round robin is a load-balancing algorithm that cycles through servers in a fixed order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把新请求发给当前活跃连接数最少的服务器的负载均衡算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Least connections is a load-balancing algorithm that sends each new request to whichever server currently has the fewest active connections.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按客户端 IP 计算哈希决定路由到哪台服务器的负载均衡算法，可用于会话保持。

q: 负载均衡算法该选？
q_en: Which load-balancing algorithm should you choose for many persistent connections?
options: 永远用轮询
IP Hash
最少连接
随机
why: 长连接不像短请求会自然消散：轮询下先起的服务器会一直背着旧连接。按活跃连接数分发能防止单机被长连接慢慢压满。
why_en: For services holding SSE or WebSocket connections use least connections, which prevents one server from gradually accumulating all the active connections.
whenOtherWins: 无状态短请求服务用轮询或随机即可——简单、且扩容加机器后流量自然流向新节点。
options_en: Always use round robin.
IP hash.
Least connections.
Random.
tradeoff: Least Connections 防止长连接堆积 vs Round Robin 简单够用

optionExplanations: 轮询按请求次数平均分配，但长连接不会自然消散，先起的服务器会一直背着旧连接越堆越重。
IP Hash 是为了让同一来源 IP 稳定落到同一后端（如会话粘性），不是用来均衡长连接数量的。

IP Hash keeps a source IP on the same backend for stickiness, not for balancing connection counts.
distributing by active connection count keeps one server from being overloaded with too many long ones.
Random shares round robin's blind spot — it ignores current connection counts, so it can end up uneven.

只有软件一种形态
云负载均衡器无法扩展
硬件 LB 已被淘汰

Only the software form exists.
Cloud load balancers cannot scale.
Hardware load balancers are obsolete.

optionExplanations: 现实里的负载均衡器分硬件、软件、云托管三种形态；LB 本身吞吐见顶时，提一句上企业级硬件设备就能带回主线。

q: 什么是可用区（availability zone）模式？
q_en: What is the availability-zone deployment pattern?
options: 把所有服务器放在一栋楼里
每个用户一台专属服务器
只在一个国家部署
同区域多个数据中心（AZ）

why_en: A region contains multiple data centers called availability zones so one building failure cannot take down the service, and the model repeats across world cities.
options_en: Put all the servers in one building.
Give every user a dedicated server.
Deploy only in one country.
Multiple data centers, called AZs, within one region.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一区域内彼此独立供电、网络的数据中心，用来抗局部故障。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An availability zone is a data center within a region that has independent power and networking so it can survive a local outage.

optionExplanations: 都放一栋楼没有任何容灾能力，一次停电或火灾就能整体挂掉，跟可用区模式的初衷相反。
每用户一台专属服务器是资源浪费，跟可用区描述的「同区域多机房分布」完全是两码事。

one dedicated server for every single user wastes resources and has nothing to do with what an AZ describes.
deploying in one country is unrelated to the AZ pattern — that's cross-region deployment instead.
the AZ pattern deploys multiple isolated data centers within a region, so one AZ failing doesn't sink it.

q: 光速给纽约-伦敦的往返延迟定了什么物理下限？
q_en: What round-trip latency lower bound does the speed of light impose between New York and London?
options: 约 1ms
往返理论最低约 56ms
约 500ms
没有物理下限，取决于带宽
why: 还没算任何处理时间，物理就先收走 56ms。这条硬约束是低延迟应用必须做地理分布的根本原因——你无法优化光速。
why_en: Light in fiber travels at about two thirds of light speed, so a New York to London round trip has a theoretical floor of roughly fifty-six milliseconds.
scenario: 设计一个跨大陆服务：客户端在纽约，一部分依赖部署在伦敦，需要估算物理延迟的下限。

options_en: About 1 millisecond.
The theoretical round-trip floor is about 56ms.
About 500 milliseconds.
There's no physical floor, it's all down to bandwidth.
optionExplanations: 1ms 远低于光速物理下限，这个量级只够本地局域网内往返。
光纤里光速打了折扣，纽约到伦敦的物理距离决定了这个往返下限。
500ms 比物理下限高出一个数量级，那是把网络拥堵也算进去的量级。
距离和光速摆在那儿，物理下限是存在的，不是单纯看带宽。
optionExplanations_en: 1ms sits far below the physical floor — that magnitude only fits a local LAN round trip.
fiber slows light below its vacuum speed, and NY-London distance sets this floor.
500ms is an order of magnitude above the floor — that's counting network congestion too.
distance and light speed are fixed, so a physical floor exists — it isn't just about bandwidth.

scenario: 数据高度可缓存、且全球各地都要查询——比如 Facebook 帖子搜索的热门结果。
scenario_en: The data is highly cacheable and queried globally, such as popular Facebook post search results.
q: 降低延迟的首选策略是？
q_en: What is the first strategy to reduce latency for globally cached data?
options: 把数据库复制到每一个国家
干脆让用户等着
CDN：边缘节点就近命中，卸后端压力
只增加服务器的 CPU
why: CDN 的前提是缓存：数据不常变/不需要频繁更新时就能放到边缘。静态资源（图片、视频）最典型，可缓存的查询结果同样适用——既降延迟又卸后端压力。
why_en: A CDN caches highly cacheable data at edge servers near users, cutting latency dramatically while also reducing load on the backend.
whenOtherWins: 高度动态、按用户各不相同、不可缓存的数据不适合 CDN——这时要靠区域化部署把计算和数据搬到用户附近。
options_en: Replicate the database into every single country.
Just make the user wait.
A CDN: edge servers serve nearby hits and take load off the backend.
Just add more server CPU.
tradeoff: CDN 缓存可复用内容 vs 区域分区处理动态本地数据

rows: 高度可缓存、少变的内容
按用户地理天然隔离的数据

termDefinitions.meaning: 遍布各地的边缘服务器网络，把可缓存内容放到离用户更近的地方。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge servers spread across locations that cache content closer to users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按地理区域拆分数据和服务，让每个区域只处理本地请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Regional partitioning splits data and services by geography so each region only handles its own local requests.

optionExplanations: 把数据库整份复制到每个国家能降延迟，但要处理多地写入一致性，对可缓存的只读查询是杀鸡用牛刀。
让用户干等不是解决方案，只是回避了问题，面试里这个选项本身就不该出现在候选方案里。
数据高度可缓存又要全球访问时，CDN 把内容放到边缘节点就近命中，既降延迟又替源站卸压力。
加 CPU 解决的是计算瓶颈，这里的延迟主要来自网络距离，堆算力对物理传输时间没有帮助。
optionExplanations_en: Fully replicating the database everywhere cuts latency but adds multi-region write consistency — overkill.
Making users wait isn't a solution, it just dodges the problem — shouldn't even be a candidate option.
when data is highly cacheable and globally accessed, a CDN serves it from edge nodes near the user.
Adding CPU addresses a compute bottleneck; the latency here comes from network distance, not compute.

scenario: Uber 式业务：迈阿密的乘客永远不会约纽约的司机——请求天然只关心本地数据。全天有百万级用户，但单个城市内只有几千。
scenario_en: In an Uber-like system, a rider in Miami will never match with a driver in New York; there are millions of users globally but only thousands per city.
q: 架构上该利用这个洞察做什么？
q_en: What architecture should you use when requests naturally only need local data?
options: 区域分区：按城市分数据库，就近处理
所有数据放一个全球主库
每个用户复制全量数据
全部靠 CDN 缓存
options_en: Regional partitioning: split the database by city and handle requests locally.
Put all data in one global primary database.
Replicate all data to every user.
Rely entirely on CDN caching.
tradeoff: 粗粒度区域路由 vs 细粒度空间索引
why: 先按城市或区域把请求路由到本地分片，再在本地分片里做附近搜索。geohash 没错，但它通常是第二层：用于在迈阿密分片内找附近司机。
why_en: First route the request to the city or regional shard, then run proximity search inside that local shard. Geohash is useful, but usually as the second layer.
whenOtherWins: 若数据必须全球共享（社交关系图、全球排行榜），不能只查本地分片；需要复制、缓存或跨区查询来处理全局视图。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  R["Miami rider request"] --> G["geo/city router"]
  G --> M["Miami regional shard"]
  G -.not needed.-> N["New York shard"]
  M --> H["geohash / spatial index"]
  H --> D["nearby Miami drivers"]

rows: 先决定查哪个本地数据集
在本地数据集中找附近对象
geohash 扫当前格和相邻格
处理城市边界或机场等灰区
额外查相邻区域或相邻格

termDefinitions.meaning: 按城市、州或区域拆数据。请求先被路由到拥有本地数据的分片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Regional sharding splits data by city, state, or region, so a request first reaches the shard that owns the local data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 这里指拥有本地区域数据的服务或数据库分片，不一定真在同一座城市。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A local node means the service or database shard that owns that region's data, not necessarily a machine physically inside the city.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把经纬度编码成网格键。它适合在某个区域内快速找附近对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash encodes latitude and longitude into grid keys, which helps find nearby objects inside a chosen region.

optionExplanations: 请求天然只关心本城市数据时，按城市分库能让绝大多数请求就近处理，而不是每次都跨城市查询。
所有数据挤进一个全球主库会让每个请求都可能跨地域访问，直接违背了「本地请求只关心本地数据」这条约束。
给每个用户复制全量数据既浪费存储也没必要——用户压根不需要其他城市的完整数据。
CDN 适合缓存不常变的内容，这里的乘客-司机匹配数据高度动态、实时变化，不适合靠缓存解决。
optionExplanations_en: when requests only care about their own city, partitioning by city serves most requests locally.
Cramming data into one global primary means any request could cross regions, breaking the locality constraint.
Replicating full data per user wastes storage and isn't necessary — users never need another city's full data.
A CDN suits content that rarely changes; rider-driver matching is too dynamic for caching alone to fix.

scenario: 用户在 LA，核心服务和数据在纽约；即使数据库查询本身很快，跨洲网络距离也会进入端到端延迟。
scenario_en: A user is in Los Angeles while the core service and data are in New York; even a fast database query still pays cross-country network distance.
q: 「数据局部性（data locality）」原则的内容是？
q_en: What does the data locality principle mean?
options: 数据必须存放在本地磁盘上
整个计算领域通用：数据离计算越近越快
每个国家各存一份数据副本
数据永远只能有一份
why: LA↔NY 约 4,000km，光纤约 200,000km/s，单程物理下限约 20ms、RTT 至少约 40ms；真实路径还会更高。数据局部性就是让一次查询需要的数据彼此靠近，并尽量靠近用户。
why_en: Data locality means keeping query data close together and near the user; LA to New York already has roughly a 40ms round-trip lower bound before routing and queueing.
options_en: Data must live on local disk.
A principle across computing: the closer data is to the computation, the faster it runs.
Every country needs its own separate data replica.
There can only ever be a single copy of the data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让计算需要的数据尽量靠近计算发生的地方（也靠近用户），以降低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Data locality means keeping the data a computation needs as close as possible to where the computation runs, and to the user.

termDefinitions.meaning: Round-Trip Time（RTT）：请求从一端到另一端再返回所需的往返时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Round-trip time is the time for a request to travel to the other side and for a response to come back.

optionExplanations: 数据局部性讲的是「数据和计算之间的物理/网络距离」，不是特指必须落在本地磁盘。
数据局部性是计算领域的通用原则——数据离用它的计算越近，网络传输时间越短，延迟越低。
每个国家一份副本是数据局部性的一种可能实现手段，但原则本身不要求必须按国家划分。
数据局部性不禁止多副本，恰恰相反，为让数据离各地用户更近，往往需要多份副本或缓存。
optionExplanations_en: data locality is about physical/network distance, not a rule requiring local disk specifically.
data locality is a general computing principle — the closer data sits to compute, the lower the latency.
one copy per country is one possible implementation, but the principle doesn't require it.
data locality doesn't forbid multiple copies — keeping data close to users often needs replicas.

scenario: 你的跨区域调用平时 100% 成功，某天光缆被挖断，大面积超时突然出现。
scenario_en: Your cross-region calls succeed a hundred percent of the time until a fiber cut suddenly causes widespread timeouts.
q: 分布式系统「最危险的假设」是哪条？正确的心态是什么？
q_en: What is the most dangerous assumption in distributed systems, and what mindset should replace it?
options: 「磁盘容量永远是无限的」这个假设
「所有时钟永远都是同步的」这个假设
「用户的行为总是理性的」这个假设
「网络是可靠的」——这条假设本身就是错的
why: 服务器会崩、比特会被宇宙射线翻转、光缆会被挖断。健壮的设计不是假设失败不发生，而是把失败当作常态来规划。
why_en: The fallacy that the network is reliable is the most dangerous assumption, so always design expecting calls to fail, be delayed, or return unexpected results.
options_en: The assumption that disk space is unlimited.
The assumption that all clocks are perfectly synchronized.
The assumption that users always behave rationally.
'The network is reliable' — that assumption itself is the dangerous one.
optionExplanations: 磁盘容量有限确实要规划，但这不是分布式系统设计里公认最危险的那条假设。
时钟不同步确实是分布式系统的经典难题，但更根本、更容易被想当然的是「网络一定能送达」。
用户行为的不确定性要在产品和校验层面处理，不是这里说的「系统基础设施层面的假设」。
服务器会崩、光缆会被挖断、比特会被翻转——「网络可靠」是最容易被想当然、也最危险的假设。
optionExplanations_en: Disk capacity being finite is a real planning concern, but not the most dangerous assumption flagged here.
unsynchronized clocks are a classic headache, but the more fundamental assumption is 'the network delivers.'
unpredictable user behavior is a product/validation concern, not an infrastructure-level assumption.
servers crash, fiber gets cut, bits flip — assuming a reliable network is the most dangerous assumption.

scenario: 下游服务偶发瞬时故障（临时变慢、偶尔超时），面试官问你怎么处理。
scenario_en: A downstream service has transient failures such as temporary slowness or occasional timeouts, and the interviewer asks how you handle them.
q: 面试官在等的「魔法短语」是？
q_en: What magic phrase is the interviewer looking for when downstream calls fail transiently?
options: 重启服务
换一个下游服务
指数退避重试
把超时设成无限大
why: 超时+重试是处理瞬时失败的基本卫生。指数退避给系统喘息、避免重试风暴；这个短语面试官明确在等，senior 级别要能展开讲 jitter。
why_en: Interviewers are often looking for the magic phrase retry with exponential backoff, and senior candidates should be ready to elaborate on adding jitter.
whenOtherWins: 被重试的 API 若非幂等（如扣款），先解决幂等性（幂等键），否则重试会造成重复副作用。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["第 1 次"] -->|失败| B["等 100ms"]
    B --> C["第 2 次"]
    C -->|失败| D["等 200ms"]
    D --> E["第 3 次"]
    E -->|失败| F["等更久"]
options_en: Restart the service.
Switch to a different downstream service.
Retry with exponential backoff.
Set the timeout to infinity.
tradeoff: 立即重试快但可能雪上加霜 vs 退避慢一点但给系统喘息
codeSample:
delay = min(cap, base * 2 ** attempt) + random(0, jitter)
# attempt=0 -> ~100ms, attempt=3 -> ~800ms + 随机抖动
# cap 防止无限拉长；jitter 避免所有客户端同一时刻齐射重试

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次重试失败后把等待时间成倍拉长的策略，给系统恢复的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exponential backoff doubles the wait time after each failed retry, giving the system room to recover.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给重试等待时间加的随机扰动，防止所有客户端同一时刻一起重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Jitter is randomness added to a retry delay so clients do not all retry at exactly the same moment.

optionExplanations: 重启服务是应对进程本身出问题的手段，跟「下游偶发瞬时故障」这种外部依赖抖动没有直接关系。
临时切换下游服务不总是可行（可能没有备选），也没解决「怎么优雅处理瞬时失败」这个通用问题。
超时配合指数退避是处理瞬时失败的标准做法——退避留出恢复窗口、防止重试打成一片，这正是面试官等的关键词。
把超时设成无限大等于放弃超时保护，请求会一直挂着占资源，跟「快速失败、优雅处理」的方向正相反。
optionExplanations_en: Restarting the service fixes a problem in the process itself, unrelated to a downstream dependency hiccup.
Switching downstream isn't always possible, and it doesn't solve handling transient failure in general.
timeout plus exponential backoff is standard hygiene; it avoids a retry storm, the phrase they listen for.
Setting the timeout to infinite gives up timeout protection entirely, the opposite of failing fast gracefully.

scenario: 下游服务已经过载在返回 500，而你的客户端配置的是立即、无限次重试。
scenario_en: A downstream service is already overloaded and returning 500s, while your client is configured to retry immediately and without limit.
q: 重试为什么是「双刃剑」？
q_en: Why are retries a double-edged sword?
options: 大量重试会反复冲击注定失败的请求，加剧问题
重试会导致数据加密直接失败
重试机制只在单机系统里才有效
重试本身会让单次请求变得更快
why: 对一个已经趴下的服务疯狂重试等于持续补刀。退避把重试的压力摊薄到时间上，把「雪上加霜」变成「给它时间恢复」。
why_en: Aggressive retries can hammer an already failing service and make things worse, which is why backoff waits progressively longer between attempts.
options_en: A flood of retries keeps hammering a request that's doomed to fail, making things worse.
Retries cause encryption to outright fail.
Retry logic only works on single-machine systems.
Retries by themselves make a single request faster.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次重试失败后把等待时间成倍拉长的策略，给系统恢复的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exponential backoff doubles the wait time after each failed retry, giving the system room to recover.

optionExplanations: 对一个撑不住的服务持续发起重试，等于不断在它身上补刀，退避就是把这股冲击摊薄到时间线上，给恢复留窗口。
重试跟数据加密是完全不相关的两件事，重试不会影响加密流程。
重试机制在分布式系统里同样常见（甚至更需要），不是单机系统专属的技术。
重试本身不会让单次请求变快，它只是失败后再试一次，整体反而因等待和退避变慢。
optionExplanations_en: hammering an already-struggling service with retries just keeps piling on, turning a hiccup into a collapse.
retries and data encryption are entirely unrelated — retrying doesn't affect the encryption pipeline.
retry logic is just as common (or more needed) in distributed systems, not single-machine-only.
retrying doesn't make one request faster — it just tries again, and overall latency actually grows.

scenario: 一次下游抖动让 10 万客户端同时失败，而它们用的是完全相同的指数退避参数。
scenario_en: One downstream blip fails a hundred thousand clients at the same instant, and they all run identical exponential backoff parameters.
q: 退避策略里为什么必须掺入随机性（jitter）？
q_en: Why must a backoff strategy include jitter?
options: 为了让日志更好看
防止所有客户端同一时刻同步重试
为了绕过限流
随机性能提升单个请求成功率
why: 没有 jitter，指数退避会让所有客户端的重试波峰完美对齐、一次次齐射。加随机把波峰摊平，才真正给系统留出恢复窗口。
why_en: Jitter adds randomness so clients do not synchronize their retries into repeated simultaneous bursts hammering the service like a jackhammer.
options_en: To make the logs look nicer.
It stops every client from synchronizing their retries at the same instant.
To bypass rate limiting.
Randomness improves a single request's odds of success.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给重试等待时间加的随机扰动，防止所有客户端同一时刻一起重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Jitter is randomness added to a retry delay so clients do not all retry at exactly the same moment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次重试失败后把等待时间成倍拉长的策略，给系统恢复的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exponential backoff doubles the wait time after each failed retry, giving the system room to recover.

optionExplanations: jitter 跟日志好不好看没有关系，它是为了打散重试时机，不是格式或美观层面的考虑。
没有 jitter 所有客户端的退避会同步对齐、一次次齐射；加入随机把波峰摊平，真正给系统留出恢复窗口。
jitter 不是用来绕过限流的手段，限流是服务端主动的保护措施，跟客户端加不加随机无关。
jitter 不提升单个请求本身的成功率，它优化的是全体客户端重试请求在时间上的分布。
optionExplanations_en: jitter has nothing to do with how logs look — it's about spreading out retry timing.
without jitter, every client's backoff aligns and fires in waves; randomness flattens those spikes.
jitter isn't a way to bypass rate limiting — that's a server-side protection, unrelated to client randomness.
jitter doesn't improve any single request's odds — it optimizes how retries are spread over time.

scenario: 支付接口因网关超时被客户端重试，但首次请求其实已经在下游扣款成功。
scenario_en: A payment call is retried because the gateway timed out, but the first request had actually already charged the card downstream.
q: 支付接口 charge $10 遇到重试，怎么防止把用户扣成 $20 甚至 $2,000？
q_en: How do you prevent a retried $10 charge from becoming $20 or $2,000?
options: 从源头上直接禁止一切重试行为
要求每次重试之前都必须人工确认
引入幂等键：请求的唯一标识，服务端靠它去重
在扣款成功后立刻主动发起一笔退款
why: 读天然幂等（GET），写要自己构造幂等：幂等键让服务器识别重复请求。友好的实现会等首个请求完成后把结果发给所有等待者，不友好的直接报「请求已存在」——但都不会重复扣款。
why_en: An idempotency key uniquely identifies the request so the server processes it only once, preventing retries from double charging the user.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: pay(key=K)
    S-->>C: timeout
    C->>S: retry pay(key=K)
    S-->>C: 返回同一结果
    Note over S: K 已处理，不重复扣款
options_en: Forbid all retries outright, from the source.
Require manual confirmation before every single retry attempt.
Introduce an idempotency key that uniquely identifies the request so the server can dedupe.
Immediately trigger a refund right after the charge succeeds.
codeSample:
POST /payments HTTP/1.1
Idempotency-Key: user_42_2026-07-02

# 服务端记录该 key 的处理结果；同一个 key 重试直接返回首次结果，不再扣款

termDefinitions.meaning: 标识一次请求的唯一键，服务端靠它识别并拒绝重复执行同一请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotency key uniquely identifies a request so the server can recognize and refuse to re-execute a duplicate.

optionExplanations: 禁止重试会牺牲重试本该解决的可用性，遇到偶发网络抖动请求直接失败，不是好方案。
人工确认在真实高并发场景下完全不现实，重试往往是毫秒级的自动行为，等不起人工介入。
给每个请求带上唯一的幂等键，服务端靠它识别「这笔扣款是不是已经处理过」，重复请求也只扣一次款。
扣款后再退款是先犯错再补救，用户体验和资金流都要多绕一圈，不如从源头防止重复扣款。
optionExplanations_en: Banning retries gives up the availability retries exist for — a brief hiccup just fails the request outright.
Manual confirmation is unrealistic at real concurrency — retries fire in milliseconds, no time for a human.
a unique idempotency key lets the server recognize a charge was already processed, so it only charges once.
Charging then refunding fixes the mistake after the fact, an extra round trip better prevented at the source.

q: 把熔断器（circuit breaker）的工作流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the circuit breaker workflow in the correct order.
steps: 熔断打开期间，请求直接快速失败，不再发起真实调用
持续监控对外部服务调用的失败情况
试探请求成功则闭合电路恢复，失败则继续保持打开
失败超过阈值，熔断器「跳闸」进入 open 状态
超时之后，电路转入 half-open 半开状态
why: 监控 → 跳闸 → 快速失败 → 半开 → 试探定夺。灵感来自电气熔断器：防止级联故障蔓延，并给故障服务恢复时间。
why_en: A circuit breaker monitors failures, trips open past a threshold, fails fast while open, moves to half-open after a timeout, and a test request decides whether to close.
diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Closed: 正常调用
    Closed --> Open: 失败超过阈值，跳闸
    Open --> HalfOpen: 超时后半开
    HalfOpen --> Closed: 试探成功
    HalfOpen --> Open: 试探失败

termDefinitions.meaning: 监控对某依赖的失败率，超阈值后让请求快速失败而不再真的调用，给依赖恢复时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circuit breaker monitors failures against a dependency and, past a threshold, fails requests fast instead of calling it, giving the dependency time to recover.

scenario: 推荐服务挂了把整个首页拖死，你要让首页在 100ms 内降级返回而不是干等超时。
scenario_en: The recommendation service is down and dragging the whole home page with it, so the page must degrade within a hundred milliseconds instead of hanging on a timeout.
q: 熔断器带来哪些好处？（多选）
q_en: What benefits does a circuit breaker provide?
options: 快速失败：立刻拒绝而不是干等超时，UI 有快速兜底而非挂死
减负：不再向已经挣扎的服务倾泻更多请求
自愈：不放全量流量的情况下自动试探恢复；隔离故障、防止蔓延到整个系统
提升下游服务的最大吞吐量
why: 熔断器的价值：fail fast、给故障服务减压、半开态自动试探、把一处故障圈起来不扩散。它不会让下游更快——只是不再补刀。
why_en: Circuit breakers fail fast, reduce load on struggling services, self-heal by testing recovery, and keep one failure from cascading through the system.
options_en: Fail fast: reject immediately instead of waiting out a timeout, so the UI gets a quick fallback instead of hanging.
Reduce load: stop pouring more requests onto an already struggling service.
Self-heal by automatically probing recovery without full traffic, and isolate the failure so it doesn't cascade through the whole system.
Increase the downstream service's maximum throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 监控对某依赖的失败率，超阈值后让请求快速失败而不再真的调用，给依赖恢复时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circuit breaker monitors failures against a dependency and, past a threshold, fails requests fast instead of calling it, giving the dependency time to recover.

optionExplanations: 熔断打开后请求立刻被拒绝，不用干等一个超时周期，UI 能马上展示兜底状态而不是转圈挂死。
熔断打开意味着不再往已经喘不过气的下游倾泻新请求，替它腾出恢复的空间。
半开态会放一小部分流量去试探下游是否恢复，同时把这处故障圈住，不让它蔓延到整个系统。
熔断器不会让下游服务本身处理得更快，它只是不再往下游补刀，跟提升吞吐量是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: once tripped, requests are rejected instantly instead of waiting out a timeout, so the UI shows a fallback.
a tripped breaker means new requests stop piling onto an already-struggling downstream.
half-open state tests a slice of traffic while containing the failure so it doesn't cascade.
a breaker doesn't make downstream process faster — it just stops piling on, a different thing.

scenario: 数据库冷宕机后需要逐实例重启，但重试洪峰和愤怒用户的流量把第一个实例反复压趴（thundering herd）——第一台永远起不来，整库无法恢复。
scenario_en: After a database cold outage, instances must restart one by one, but retry floods and user traffic keep crushing the first instance before recovery can progress.
q: 预防这类级联故障的关键模式是？
q_en: What pattern prevents this cascading failure during database recovery?
options: 干脆再增加更多的重试次数
把数据库连接池调得再大一些
干脆换成一个更快的数据库
熔断器：超阈值后停止真实调用、快速失败
why: 「一个故障制造出新的故障」是级联故障的标志——识别这些模式并给出缓解，是面试脱颖而出的好方法（也是 3am oncall 的血泪结晶）。
why_en: A circuit breaker stops the retry firehose so the recovering database gets breathing room, preventing the thundering herd from pinning it down forever.
whenOtherWins: 偶发的瞬时失败用「重试+指数退避」就够；熔断器针对的是持续性故障与级联风险。
options_en: Just add even more retries on top.
Make the database connection pool even larger still.
Just switch over to a faster database.
A circuit breaker that stops real calls and fails fast past a failure threshold.
tradeoff: 持续重试雪上加霜 vs 熔断给恢复窗口

termDefinitions.meaning: 监控对某依赖的失败率，超阈值后让请求快速失败而不再真的调用，给依赖恢复时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circuit breaker monitors failures against a dependency and, past a threshold, fails requests fast instead of calling it, giving the dependency time to recover.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大量请求或重试同时压向同一个刚恢复/正在恢复的资源，反而把它再次压垮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A thundering herd is a burst of simultaneous requests or retries slamming a just-recovering resource hard enough to knock it back down.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次重试失败后把等待时间成倍拉长的策略，给系统恢复的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exponential backoff doubles the wait time after each failed retry, giving the system room to recover.

optionExplanations: 增加重试在这个场景里只会火上浇油——第一个实例本就被 thundering herd 压垮，更多重试等于更多补刀。
调大连接池能缓一时，但根源是重试洪峰持续冲击刚起来的实例，池子再大也会被同样的洪峰打满。
换更快的数据库不解决「实例刚起来就被流量压趴」这个问题，瓶颈在于流量模式而不是单机性能。
熔断器在错误率超阈值后直接停止真实调用、快速失败，给第一个实例留出不被淹没的启动窗口。
optionExplanations_en: Adding more retries here pours fuel on the fire — the first instance is already crushed by a thundering herd.
A bigger connection pool buys a little time, but a retry storm eventually overwhelms any pool size.
A faster database doesn't fix an instance getting crushed at startup — the bottleneck is the traffic pattern.
once the error rate crosses a threshold, the breaker fails fast, giving the first instance a startup window.

scenario: 你要划定微服务系统里熔断器的安装边界，同时不给无网络的调用增加开销。
scenario_en: You're deciding where circuit breakers belong in a microservice system, without adding overhead to calls that never cross the network.
q: 熔断器适合安插在哪些位置？（多选）
q_en: Where should circuit breakers be placed?
options: 对第三方外部 API 的调用
数据库连接与查询
微服务之间的服务间调用；以及任何可能失败或变慢的网络调用/重操作
进程内的纯内存函数调用
why: 原则：凡是跨网络、可能失败或变慢的依赖调用都值得熔断保护。进程内纯内存计算没有网络故障模式，不需要熔断器。
why_en: Place circuit breakers around third-party API calls, database queries, service-to-service communication, and any network call that could fail or slow down.
options_en: Calls to third-party external APIs.
Database connections and queries.
Service-to-service calls between microservices, and any network call or heavy operation that could fail or slow down.
Pure in-process, in-memory function calls.
tradeoff: 跨网络易失败的调用要熔断 vs 进程内内存调用不需要

termDefinitions.meaning: 监控对某依赖的失败率，超阈值后让请求快速失败而不再真的调用，给依赖恢复时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circuit breaker monitors failures against a dependency and, past a threshold, fails requests fast instead of calling it, giving the dependency time to recover.

optionExplanations: 调用不受你控制的第三方 API 时，对方抖动或变慢会直接拖累你的服务，值得用熔断器保护。
数据库连接和查询是典型的跨网络调用，会失败或变慢，熔断器能防止连接池被拖垮的查询占满。
只要调用跨越网络边界、有失败或变慢的可能（服务间调用、耗时操作），都在熔断器的保护范围内。
进程内的纯内存函数调用不跨网络，没有「对方变慢/掉线」这种故障模式，套熔断器只是多余开销。
optionExplanations_en: calling a third-party API you don't control means their hiccups drag your service down too.
database connections and queries can fail or slow down, and a breaker stops queries from hogging the pool.
any dependency call crossing the network that can fail or slow down fits within a breaker's scope.
an in-process, in-memory call never crosses the network, so a breaker there is needless overhead.
